compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

`infra/scripts/docker-storage-cap.sh` `effective_gc_verdict` reads BuildKit's effective GC ceiling from `docker buildx inspect` with a `sed` that matches only `Keep Bytes:` lines. Both the `--install` read-back (`report_effective_gc_policy`) and the every-tick `--check-gc-enforced` probe behind the `docker_buildkit_gc_enforced` metric and the `rebar-docker-buildkit-gc-not-enforced` alarm use it.

From buildx v0.18.0, `inspect` no longer prints `Keep Bytes:`. On any host whose buildx CLI plugin is v0.18.0 or later, the parser finds nothing, the verdict is "unreadable" (return 2), `--check-gc-enforced` prints nothing, and the metric reads unknown permanently. buildx is a CLI plugin versioned independently of dockerd, so a package update alone triggers this. Not live: rebar-gerrit still prints `Keep Bytes:`.

Evidence (primary sources):
- docker/buildx `commands/inspect.go` at v0.17.0 prints `\tKeep Bytes:\t%s` from `rule.KeepBytes`. At v0.18.0 it prints `\tReserved Space:\t%s`, `\tMax Used Space:\t%s` and `\tMin Free Space:\t%s`, each only when non-zero, all via go-units `BytesSize` (`%.4g` + binary suffix, e.g. `5GiB`). The change is buildx commit 64c5139ab6 (2024-10-08), first tagged in v0.18.0. https://github.com/docker/buildx/blob/v0.18.0/commands/inspect.go
- The buildx reference doc `docs/reference/buildx_inspect.md` still shows `Keep Bytes:` at v0.18.0 through main. The doc contradicts the source, and the source is what runs, so test fixtures follow `inspect.go`.
- moby/buildkit `api/types/worker.proto`: v0.16.0 field 3 is `keepBytes`. v0.17.0 renames field 3 to `reservedSpace` and adds `maxUsedSpace` = 5 and `minFreeSpace` = 6. So buildx >= 0.18 against an old daemon (BuildKit 0.12.6, as on production) shows the old keep-bytes as `Reserved Space:`.
- BuildKit v0.20.0 `cache/manager.go` `calculateKeepBytes`: keep = maxUsedSpace, lowered by the min-free excess, then raised to at least reservedSpace. So a rule's upper bound is `max(reservedSpace, maxUsedSpace)`, and `minFreeSpace` only ever lowers it. The widest ceiling over all rules is therefore the largest value on any `Keep Bytes:`, `Reserved Space:` or `Max Used Space:` line. `Min Free Space:` is a disk-free floor, not a cache size, and must be excluded.

## Approach

Widen the one existing extractor rather than add a second parser. In `effective_gc_verdict`, change the `sed` expression to capture the value after `Keep Bytes:`, `Reserved Space:` or `Max Used Space:` (case-insensitive first letters, as today). The Python comparison needs no change. Both shapes print the same value format: buildx v0.17.0 `inspect.go:126` already formats `Keep Bytes:` with `units.BytesSize(float64(rule.KeepBytes))`, the same go-units `BytesSize` (e.g. `5.588GiB`) that v0.18.0 uses for the three new labels. The existing `as_bytes` in the heredoc (`docker-storage-cap.sh:211-218`, `UNITS` with `b`, `kb`...`tb`, `kib`...`tib`) already parses that format, and the existing live-host test `test_check_gc_enforced_prints_0_on_the_live_host_shape` feeds it `5.588GiB`. It already takes the largest captured size, so the widest-rule semantics stay unchanged for legacy output. `Min Free Space:` is deliberately not matched. Then update the surrounding comments, the "keep-bytes" wording in the three read-back warnings, and the `--check-gc-enforced` header, so they name both output shapes. `--install` and `--check-gc-enforced` share this function, so both are fixed by one edit.

`infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md`: the diagnostic `grep -E 'Buildkit|Keep Bytes'` also matches the new labels.

Out of scope: `infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf` alarm descriptions that say "Keep Bytes". Editing them makes a Terraform diff that only an apply clears, and production is read-only here.

## Scope

- `infra/scripts/docker-storage-cap.sh` — the `effective_gc_verdict` extractor, its comments and the read-back warnings.
- `tests/scripts/test_docker_storage_cap.py` — a buildx >= 0.18 inspect fixture in `_bindir`'s `docker` stub (new `inspect_shape` keyword, default the current legacy shape) and the new tests.
- `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md` — the diagnostic grep.

## Testing

Written first, failing on the current tree. The new fixture reproduces v0.18.0 `inspect.go` output for a Docker-driver builder: tab-separated labels, rule#0 filtered with `Max Used Space` (small temp-cache cap), and rules #1-#3 with `Reserved Space` only (the Engine 25-27 / BuildKit <= 0.16 daemon mapping, and the Engine 28 `defaultKeepStorage` mapping):
- `--check-gc-enforced` prints `1` when the widest `Reserved Space` is 5GiB.
- It prints `0` on the production value (5.588GiB) in the new shape.
- It prints `1` when the widest ceiling is a `Max Used Space` of 5GiB with a smaller `Reserved Space`.
- A `Min Free Space: 5GiB` line beside a `Reserved Space: 20GiB` gives `0` (min-free not counted).
- A new-shape output with no space lines prints nothing and exits non-zero (unreadable).
- `--install` read-back over the new shape warns "IS being enforced" on a match and "does NOT match" on a mismatch.
- Every existing legacy `Keep Bytes:` test passes unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `--check-gc-enforced` prints `1`, `0` or nothing for the buildx >= 0.18 fixtures in the Testing section. Verified by the new tests in `tests/scripts/test_docker_storage_cap.py`.
- [x] The `--install` read-back reports enforced or mismatch over the buildx >= 0.18 fixture. Verified by the new tests.
- [x] A `Min Free Space:` value never counts as the ceiling. Verified by the min-free test.
- [x] Legacy `Keep Bytes:` output gives the same verdicts as before. Verified by the existing `--check-gc-enforced` and read-back tests passing unmodified.
- [x] `.venv/bin/pytest tests/scripts/test_docker_storage_cap.py` passes.
- [x] `make lint` exits 0, with the worktree `.venv/bin` first on PATH.
- [x] `make typecheck` exits 0, with the worktree `.venv/bin` first on PATH.
- [x] [non-codebase] The change lands on `main` through Gerrit with `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`.
